cities.name: Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair)
cities.overview: The capital of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, renamed from Port Blair in 2024, and the arrival point for flights and ferries.

cities.name: Swaraj Dweep (Havelock)
cities.overview: The most popular island for beaches and diving, about two hours by ferry from Sri Vijaya Puram; renamed from Havelock Island in 2018.

places.name: Cellular Jail
places.shortDescription: The colonial prison known as Kala Pani, where freedom fighters were held in solitary cells, now a national memorial.
places.description: The Cellular Jail was built with seven wings radiating from a central tower, each lined with tiny solitary cells so no prisoner could see another. Three wings survive, along with the gallows, a museum and photo gallery about the freedom fighters held here, among them V. D. Savarkar and Batukeshwar Dutt. The evening light-and-sound show in the courtyard tells the jail's story. Climb the central tower for views over the harbour and Ross Island.
places.history: The British built the jail between 1896 and 1906 to hold political prisoners exiled from the mainland, a punishment known as Kala Pani. It was declared a national memorial in 1979.

entryFee.note: Small entry fee; the light-and-sound show is ticketed separately.

timings.hours: About 9:00 AM – 12:30 PM and 1:30 PM – 4:45 PM; closed Mondays

location.address: Atlanta Point, Sri Vijaya Puram, Andaman and Nicobar Islands 744104

places.name: Ross Island (Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Dweep)
places.shortDescription: The former British administrative headquarters of the Andamans, now atmospheric ruins wrapped in tree roots.
places.description: A short boat ride from Sri Vijaya Puram, this small island was once the seat of British rule in the Andamans, with a church, bakery, ballroom, hospital and the chief commissioner's residence. Today the buildings stand roofless, overgrown by the roots of giant trees, while spotted deer and peacocks wander the lawns. A small museum explains the island's history, and an evening light-and-sound show is held on some days. Boats leave from the Aberdeen jetty.
places.history: The British occupied the island from 1858; it was damaged by an earthquake in 1941 and occupied by Japan during the Second World War. Subhas Chandra Bose hoisted the Indian tricolour in the islands in December 1943, and the island was renamed after him in 2018.

entryFee.note: Small entry fee plus boat fare from Aberdeen jetty.

timings.hours: Daytime; boats run roughly 8:30 AM – 2:00 PM

location.address: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Dweep, near Sri Vijaya Puram, Andaman and Nicobar Islands

places.name: Radhanagar Beach
places.shortDescription: A broad arc of white sand and clear turquoise water on Swaraj Dweep, regularly ranked among Asia's best beaches.
places.description: Radhanagar (Beach No. 7) curves for about 2 km along the west coast of Swaraj Dweep, backed by tall forest. The sand is fine and white, the water clear and gentle in season, and sunsets here are famous. Lifeguards patrol a marked swimming area; take care with currents outside it. A short walk north leads to the secluded Neil's Cove. The beach holds the Blue Flag certification for cleanliness and safety.
places.history: Time magazine named Radhanagar the best beach in Asia in 2004. The island was renamed from Havelock to Swaraj Dweep in 2018.
places.bestTimeNote: November to April; seas are rough during the monsoon.

location.address: Radhanagar Beach, Swaraj Dweep, South Andaman, Andaman and Nicobar Islands 744211
